_note: One readable sentence per lesson day, for the syllabus PDF.
lessons.json carries the raw recording titles joined by ' · '. Six of those
joined together is accurate but unreadable — 'Intro from PMs · Intro from LT ·
Intro to AI Engineering · Python I · Python II · Git intro + how to work in labs'.
These sentences say the same thing in a form a student can scan.
Written by hand from the titles in data/lessons.json, not generated. If a lesson
id is missing here, scripts/build_syllabus_pdf.py falls back to the raw title and
prints a warning, so a corpus change degrades rather than breaks.
w1d1: Kickoff — program intro, first steps in Python, and setting up Git for lab work.
w1d2: Python functions in depth — parameters, return values, scope, lambda functions, and list comprehensions.
w1d3: Using LLMs to learn effectively, then error handling and functional tools — map, filter, and reduce.
w1d4: Foundations for ML — tensors and linear algebra, NumPy, Pandas, and descriptive statistics.
w1d5: Grouping and merging data in Pandas, AI coding assistants, data visualization, Agile/Scrum basics, and object-oriented programming.
w2d1: Introduction to machine learning, with live demos of linear and logistic regression.
w2d2: Evaluating models — regression and classification metrics — and an overview of ML algorithms.
w2d3: A full supervised learning workflow — from problem definition and EDA through feature engineering to final evaluation.
w2d4: Unsupervised learning — clustering and dimensionality reduction with PCA.
w3d1: Deep learning foundations — neurons, activation functions, backpropagation, and a first Keras model on MNIST.
w3d2: Computer vision — image preprocessing and convolutional neural networks.
w3d4: Deploying models with Gradio, and improving them with data augmentation and transfer learning.
w4d2: NLP fundamentals — tokenization, stemming, TF-IDF, and a news-clustering example.
w5d1: Databases — SQLite setup, CRUD operations, and table relationships.
w5d2: Transformer architecture, APIs, and prompt engineering.
w5d3: Using the OpenAI API, prompt injection, and tool calling.
w5d4: Connecting to AI models, quantization, and the geopolitics of AI.
w5d5: Mini-project demos, plus transfer learning with LoRA and QLoRA.
w6d1: Building and deploying a full-stack AI app — a FastAPI backend on Render and a React frontend on Vercel.
w7d3: LangChain memory, RAG pipelines, and retrieval agents.
w7d4: Streaming responses, tool calling, and open models.
w7d5: Week recap and the IronStore mini-project.
w8d1: Multimodal search with CLIP and multimodal RAG.
